name: Prompt part: the 'Keep:' list of every prop, with its look and state

computable_from: check file groups that show (facts: visible and over about 0.1% of the frame), their role (subject, story, work, landmark) and a short painter description and state per group

calculator: Painter's request builder and plate preflight

Shot-specific: removed parts ('a handle on the pail') and library props a painter might add ('no coal tub, rails, barrel, crates or litter').

proposed_calculation: Core list + 'a <part> on the <group>' for every removed part + 'no <names>' for library props of the same place absent from the shot; replace 'people' with 'Add no people and remove none' when figures are present.

llm_tip: Always forbid new light effects and shadows; the film draws them live.

calculator: Painter's request builder and plate preflight
name: Which near things need a behind painting, and when the handover starts
how_found: Log 29: moving the camera uncovered pale jagged outlines behind the sacks and cart (lesson 91); the handover waited for 1.4 degrees, too late; half a degree works (lesson 96); every near prop then needs a soft 3D shadow (the barrel seemed to float).
final_value_or_rule: projected-set behind: { painting, hide } with reach 0.05 of the frame height round the props and quickMove 0.00003 (1 - cos of about half a degree); frontStretch [1.3, 1.9]; each hidden prop gets a soft contact shadow.
computable_from: the slide vector and each group's depth and the depth of what is behind it
proposed_calculation: parallax_px = f*L_lateral_component*|1/d_prop - 1/d_behind|/... (screen shift of the prop against the background over the slide); every group with over 1 px goes into 'hide', keep_painted_shadows and the behind prompt; every group in 'hide' gets a soft shadow automatically.
already_automatic: No; lists are typed by hand.
llm_tip: Anything the camera moves past at a different depth from its background needs the behind painting and its own soft shadow.

name: Plate preparation: thin parts and things the painter misreads

final_value_or_rule: Parts thinner than about 6 px at 1080 (the checker's without_wires opening) are removed, thickened, or named in the prompt as 'stay thin or left out'.
computable_from: solo masks from shot_facts.py
proposed_calculation: For each group: thin = solo mask minus its morphological opening (size max(3, round(6*W/1080)) odd); if thin pixels > 5% of the group, list it for removal or for the prompt's thin-parts sentence.
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: Before painting, find every wire, rung and bar under 6 px wide; remove what doesn't matter and protect the rest in the prompt.

calculator: Painter's request builder and plate preflight
name: What the painter garbles: lettering, thin parts, glows, holes
how_found: Log 29: the first repaint garbled the notice's small print, and the painter added snow-like blotches. Log 30: every program garbled the notice. Log 31: the pail's thin wire handle was removed (the painter would smear it). Log 32: an even orange disc in the drum's mouth would be painted as soup or a lid, so its glow fades up from the coals; a pure-black doorway made the shut gate read as open, so dim doors went behind it; the prompt forbade adding flames, smoke, glows or new shadows round near props, and the painter added nothing.
final_value_or_rule: Signs keep their own surfaces (ownSurface). Remove parts only a few pixels thin. No even bright discs or pure-black holes near the story. The prompt says keep every shape and the light and dark, and never add flames, smoke, glows or new shadows.
computable_from: the plate render, the shot_facts id pictures and the text sizes
proposed_calculation: A painter-readiness scan of the plate: (a) for each prop part, the thinnest it shows on screen (a distance transform of its id mask); under 3 px means remove or thicken; (b) any lettering under about 24 px tall goes on its own surface; (c) any area over 0.3% of the frame that is very even (spread under 2 levels) and strongly coloured, or under 5 levels dark, inside the story box is flagged; (d) the prompt template adds the 'never add' sentence by itself.
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: Treat any painter as a smudger of detail: keep lettering and thin parts on your own surfaces.

computable_from: render log + check_shot report

calculator: Painter's request builder and plate preflight
name: Plate preflight before paying for a painting
how_found: Logs 29-34: flames in the plate read as paper cones (89); a glowing hollow became a band (138); shadow-buffer faults (110); striped textures (round 3); maker's label on a Poly Haven texture (round 1).
final_value_or_rule: Before a paid repaint the plate must render cleanly (no shadow-memory faults), pass the light rules, have no flames or glowing hollows, no striped surfaces, no stray lettering.
evidence: Workflows.md 'Checking a shot' ('Before a paid repaint ...'); Lessons 89, 110, 138; check-round-3/tools/find_stripes.py
computable_from: plate PNG, render log, shot_facts masks, exported glb files
proposed_calculation: preflight_plate.py: grep render log for 'Shadow buffer full'/'Could not allocate shadow atlas'; run find_stripes on all glbs (faces whose UV area / 3D area < 1e-3 of the median); flag saturated bright pixels (V > 0.85, S > 0.6) inside the top 30% of any hollow prop's mask; run check_shot light rules; fail on any.

calculator: Painter's request builder and plate preflight
name: Head-back darker than the coat (no bald heads)
how_found: Round 1 check: at plate size the men from behind had pale bald-looking heads (hand-on-bar head 80/54/35 vs coat 39/25/14); the figures helper had judged 'from behind: yes'. Round 2 cast rays and read pixels: hair present but shiny, reflecting sky and lamps (22 to 25 vs cap and coat 7 to 12).
final_value_or_rule: Matt dark hair covering back and sides from under the cap into the collar; turned-up collars or high mufflers so no neck shows; caps 1.5 cm lower. Measured after: head band 12 vs coat 25, 15 vs 28 (head darker than coat).
evidence: round1-result.json checked.findings[0]; round2-result.json figures.summary and tested; KIT/paper-film/blender/figures/build_figures.py
computable_from: the plate and each figure's outline from shot facts
proposed_calculation: For each figure seen from behind: mean luminance of the band just below the cap vs mean of the coat inside its outline in the plate; flag if head >= coat. Also add a contact-sheet view lit from the camera's side (the light that showed the fault).
already_automatic: No (figure_sheet.py got the extra lamp-lit back view, but no measure).
llm_tip: Check the back of every head in the plate at full size: if it is paler than the coat, the painter will paint a face or a dummy.

calculator: Painter's request builder and plate preflight
name: Film grade turns dark cloth red: pick cloth colours after the grade
how_found: Round 2 check sampled the film: tan coats in the plate came out crimson (26/1/0, hue pure red). Round 3 found why: the film's grade turns anything darker than about 28/255 black, removing green and blue. Re-coloured, re-filmed a still and sampled again.
final_value_or_rule: Use slate grey or grey cloth that reads dull grey-brown in the warm plate (about 46/39/32); on film it samples 27/16/3 and 30/16/3 (olive brown, hue about 30 deg), not red (was 19/1/1 and 23/2/1).
evidence: round2-result.json checked.findings[3]; round3-result.json fixes.summary 'The two right-hand men's coats'
computable_from: plate colours and the stage's tone curve (cinema-stage.js grade)
proposed_calculation: Run every figure's (and every large prop's) mean plate colour through the stage's grade function; flag if the graded hue moves more than 25 deg or lands in 345-15 deg (red) / party or chain hues with saturation > 0.5; suggest the plate colour whose graded result is the wanted hue.
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: Judge colours of dark things on a filmed still, not the plate: the grade crushes dark browns to red.

calculator: Painter's request builder and plate preflight
name: Figure look checks: head backs darker than coats, coats not turned red by the grade
how_found: Log 34 round 1: heads from behind measured 80/54/35 against coats 39/25/14 and read as bald dummies; round 2: tan coats came out deep crimson (26/1/0) through the film grade.
final_value_or_rule: Dark matt hair from cap to collar, collars up, caps low; dull grey-brown or olive coats with low saturation; women bare-headed with shawls on shoulders (a hooded shawl read as a nun).

computable_from: plate or film still plus shot_facts solo masks per figure (head-back region = top 12% of the figure mask)
proposed_calculation: For each figure: mean RGB of head-back region vs coat region; flag if head luminance > 1.3x coat. Run one still through the stage finish and flag coat pixels with saturation > 0.5 and hue within 20 deg of pure red.
already_automatic: No. build_figures.py encodes the fixes by design; no measuring check.
llm_tip: Look at people at the plate's full size and through the film's colour finish; the grade pushes warm browns to red.

calculator: Painter's request builder and plate preflight
name: Faces lit from the camera side (people check)

computable_from: figure .glb files + planned distance

calculator: Painter's request builder and plate preflight
name: Nothing round sits above a collar (things that read as people)
how_found: Round 1: a hung jacket with the cap above the collar read as a headless or hunched man; round 2 hung the cap on its own nail (reads as a disc from the side); round 3 collar and slumped shoulders, cap turned; round 4 critic still read a flat disc; set helper turned it 30 deg.

evidence: round1-result.json checked.findings[3]; round2-result.json props_fixes.summary; round3-result.json fixes.summary; assemble_works.py line 1123 (CAP_TURN = -30.0)

name: Line the painting up with the plate
how_found: Lesson 123: Flux returned the notice corner 0.65% larger and 3 px off; shone back, every painted edge would sit beside the real one. align_painting.py lined it up: 96% of outlines on the painting's edges vs 70% before.
final_value_or_rule: Run align_painting.py on every painting (and --against for the behind painting).
computable_from: check file + plate facts + painting
proposed_calculation: Already computed. Make it fail if fewer than 85% of outlines line up after warping.

llm_tip: Never project a painting without lining it up first.

name: Lining a painting up with its plate
how_found: Log 32: the shot checker's new test showed every prop lining up better once slid about 4 px. The painter had stretched the picture by 0.65% and shifted it 3 px. align_painting.py undoes it: 96% of outlines then sit on the painting's edges, against 70% before.
final_value_or_rule: Always line up the main painting with its plate, then the behind painting against the lined-up main one. Aim for 95% or more of outlines on edges.
computable_from: the plate's shot facts and the painting
proposed_calculation: Already a calculation: the scale and shift that best fit the props' outlines to the painting's edges.
already_automatic: Yes, align_painting.py (plugin kit). Run by hand.
llm_tip: Run align_painting on every painting before projecting it; even 3 px shows as double edges.

name: Lining a painting up with its plate (align_painting.py)
how_found: Log 32: every prop lined up better slid about 4 px; Flux had stretched the notice corner 0.65% and shifted it 3 px (lesson 123).
final_value_or_rule: Coarse search: stretch 0.985 to 1.015 in 0.0025 steps, shift -12 to +12 px in 2 px steps (frame basis 1080 wide); fine: +-0.002 in 0.0005 and +-2 px in 0.5. Edges as above, widened 5 x 5. Results: notice corner 1.0065, +3, +3 (outlines on edges 0.70 to 0.96); people test 1.0010, +1.0, +0.5 (0.874 to 0.903).
computable_from: the painting, the plate camera's facts (shot_facts.py with the plate's lens)
proposed_calculation: Run automatically on every returned painting; accept if agreement >= 0.85 and stretch within 1%; else re-ask the painter.
already_automatic: Tool exists in the kit and plugin kit; run by hand.
llm_tip: Always line a painting up with its plate before shining it onto the set; measure the facts with the plate's own lens (64.4).

name: Painting alignment to the plate (align_painting.py)
how_found: Log 32: the checker's 'out of date' test showed every prop lining up better slid about 4 px; Flux had stretched the plate 0.65% and shifted it 3 px; aligned, 96% of outlines sat on painting edges vs 70%. People test: 1.0010x, +1/+0.5 px, 0.874 -> 0.903. Lesson 123.
final_value_or_rule: Every painting is resized to the plate (1536x2730) and aligned against the props' outlines measured by shot_facts for the plate camera and lens (64.4 deg); the behind painting aligned --against the aligned main painting; aim >= 0.90 of outlines on edges.
evidence: film-kit/paper-film/tools/align_painting.py docstring; people-test-paintings.json 'lined_up'; Workflows.md 'A built place, painted over' step 4
computable_from: painting, plate facts (shot_facts.py --camera-at ... --fov PLATE_LENS), check file
proposed_calculation: Already a calculation; make it a mandatory step that fails if the post-alignment edge share < 0.85.
already_automatic: Yes; the file is in the plugin kit (identical) but no plugin skill mentions it, and it needs shot_facts plus a check file the plugin does not ship.
llm_tip: Always run align_painting.py on every returned painting before shining it onto the set; painters shift and stretch by a few pixels.

name: Painting size and line-up
how_found: People test ledger: Flux returned 1504 x 2672 at '2k'; resized to the plate and lined up with align_painting.py against the props' outlines from shot_facts.py at the plate's own lens (64.4). Log 32 found 0.65% stretch and 3 px.
final_value_or_rule: Resize to the plate (1536 x 2730), then align: stretch 1.0010 and shift +1.0, +0.5 px; outline agreement 0.874 before, 0.903 after. The behind painting aligned with --against the lined-up painting (0.999). Keep the painting lossless (PNG).
computable_from: plate, painting, shot facts outlines
proposed_calculation: Already automatic: align_painting.py; make it a required step that refuses to continue if agreement after < 0.85 or stretch > 1%.
already_automatic: Yes (align_painting.py in film kit and plugin kit); not enforced.
llm_tip: Line up every painting with its plate before any other step; Flux shifts and stretches slightly.

name: Lining up the behind painting against the main one
how_found: Log 32 and people test.
final_value_or_rule: --against: edges of the lined-up painting (Canny 40/100 on lightness) except round the removed props (their outlines widened 25 x 25 px). Notice corner 0.990 to 0.991 (shift -0.5, -1.0); people test 0.999.
computable_from: both paintings and the near groups
proposed_calculation: Run automatically after every behind painting, naming the same groups that were painted out.
already_automatic: Tool exists; run by hand.

name: Keep painted shadows in the behind painting
how_found: Lesson 122: the painter removed the props' shadows with the props, so they faded off the pavement 2 s into the slide. Lesson 125: keeping them left a pale strip round the pail, since the gap round each prop had no shadow. Fix: carry the darkening into the gap.
final_value_or_rule: keep_painted_shadows.py: main painting everywhere except inside the near props' outlines widened 10 px, soft join, darkened inward.
computable_from: check file + plate facts + both paintings
proposed_calculation: Already computed; run it automatically after align_painting --against.
already_automatic: Yes (plugin kit has the tool; no skill mentions it).
llm_tip: The props-removed painting always needs its shadows put back.

name: Keeping painted shadows when the film switches to the behind painting
how_found: Log 32 motion check: 2 seconds in, the fire's long shadows from the pail and chair faded off the pavement. Fixed by keeping the main painting except inside the props' own outlines (keep_painted_shadows.py). A fresh helper then found a pale 10 to 15 px outline round the pail (the gap had no shadow); the shadows' darkening was carried into the gap. The pavement patch stayed at 70 to 71 levels, where before it rose to 89. Log 29: the barrel's painted scorch ring faded, so a soft 3D shadow was put under it.
final_value_or_rule: Main painting everywhere except inside near props' outlines widened 10 px; shadow darkening carried inward; soft 3D contact shadows under props whose painted shadow goes.
computable_from: the plates, the paintings and the props' outlines
proposed_calculation: Already a calculation. Add a check: pavement brightness just beside each prop, before and after the handover, changes by at most 2 levels.
already_automatic: Yes, keep_painted_shadows.py (plugin kit). Run by hand.
llm_tip: Measure the ground beside each near prop across the switch; a fading shadow shows only in motion.

name: Keeping painted shadows round the near props (keep_painted_shadows.py)
how_found: Log 32: the fire's shadows of the pail and chair faded off the pavement 2 s into the slide (lesson 122); the first fix left a pale 10 to 15 px strip round the pail (lesson 125); pavement held at 70 to 71 (was rising to 89).
final_value_or_rule: Main painting everywhere except inside the near props' outlines widened 10 px (painting pixels), soft join sigma widen/3; inside, the behind painting darkened by the ratio painting/behind (plus 8, clipped 0.25 to 1, blurred 3) measured outside and spread inward (quarter size, Telea radius 12, blurred 4). Default groups: subject, support, story props and 'lamp post'.
computable_from: check file core groups and the plate facts; which props are near enough to need it
proposed_calculation: Default groups = every group whose parallax over the slide exceeds 1 px (see the behind-painting item) instead of the hard-coded 'lamp post'; widen = the painter's outline width (measure the dark rim width round props, about 10 px).
already_automatic: Tool exists in kit and plugin kit; groups partly hard-coded.
llm_tip: After a behind painting, always keep the main painting's shadows outside the near props, then check the film frame by frame for a pale rim.

name: Keep painted shadows in the behind painting (keep_painted_shadows.py)
how_found: Log 32: the long shadows from pail and chair faded off the pavement 2 s into the slide; first fix left a pale 10-15 px outline round the pail; third filming clean (pavement patch 70-71 levels vs 89). Lessons 122, 125.
final_value_or_rule: Main painting everywhere except inside near props' own outlines widened 10 px; behind painting inside, with soft join and shadow darkening carried inward.
computable_from: check file, plate facts, painting, behind painting
proposed_calculation: Already automatic; add to the plugin's paint step and to a pipeline script.
already_automatic: Yes (in plugin kit, identical), undocumented in plugin skills.
llm_tip: After painting the props out, run keep_painted_shadows.py, then film the slide and compare a pavement patch's brightness across the handover.

name: Handing a painted set over to the 'behind' painting (ghost outlines)
how_found: Log 29: moving the camera uncovered the painter's outlines of the sacks and cart left on the road (pale jagged copies, then dark ink lines). Fixed with a props-removed painting handed over round the props as soon as the camera moves. Finding why the handover didn't work took three tries: it waited for too much camera movement, and a helper step was half thrown away by leftover depth in a working picture. Painted clouds had nowhere to land, then the sky showed a pale double edge, so the painted sky went alone on a far card.
final_value_or_rule: projected-set.js defaults: the behind painting is used round near props out to reach 0.05 of the frame height, handed over at quickMove 0.00003 (about half a degree); seam fades full at moveAngle 0.01 (about 8 degrees); frontStretch [1.3, 1.9]; edgeWidth 0.006; stretch [2.5, 5]; frameEdge 0.03; unseen surfaces darken 0.75, tint 0.6, fill 0.35; sky on its own far card.
evidence: story L946-955 (log 29), L322 and L325 (word list); film-kit/paper-film/scenes/projected-set.js lines 512-545
computable_from: the set and the plates
proposed_calculation: Keep the defaults. Work out reach from the measured width of the painter's outlines: reach = (outline px + 10 px) / H.
already_automatic: Yes in the film kit's projected-set.js. NOT in the plugin kit (the plugin has only painted-projection.js).
llm_tip: Hand over to the behind painting at the first movement, not after a threshold.

name: Behind picture for what near props hid
how_found: Lesson 91: moving the camera uncovered pale jagged copies of the coal sacks' and cart's outlines. Fix: a second painting with near props painted out, worn by those surfaces, and warm light at the fire. Workflows log 34: make_behind_picture.py is the free fill; make_state_picture.py from a helper plate is truer.
final_value_or_rule: Every near prop with a moving camera needs a behind picture.
computable_from: plate facts outlines + main painting (or helper plate)
proposed_calculation: Already computed (inpaint widened 10 px, radius 9; lossless PNG; checked equal outside).
already_automatic: In the film kit only (make_behind_picture.py and make_state_picture.py are NOT in the plugin kit).
llm_tip: Plan the behind picture with the plate; it is half the repaint cost.

name: Painted figures keep their outlines (people test result)
how_found: Paid people test (log 34, about 85 cents): plate painted by Flux 3 edit, then measured each figure's outline against the plate's (shape-match and outline distance per figure).
final_value_or_rule: Near men: painted outline matched the plate's at IoU 0.88 to 0.92, median outline error 1 px, 91 to 99.9% of outline points within 3 px; small walkers 63 to 99% within 3 px. Silhouette version contrast ratio 2.98 against 2.2 painted.
computable_from: plate outlines (shot facts) and the painting
proposed_calculation: After every painting: per figure, chamfer distance from plate outline to painting edges; flag a figure if within-3-px share < 0.90 (near) or < 0.70 (far) or IoU < 0.85, meaning the painter moved, added or lost it.
already_automatic: No (scratch scripts).
llm_tip: After a painting comes back, measure every figure's outline against the plate; a figure that moved more than 3 px has been redrawn.

name: Count figures and props in a painting against the plate
how_found: Plan 34: 'Caught by counting the figures in each painting against the plate's outlines (the shot checker lists each figure as a prop)'.
final_value_or_rule: Each figure is its own group; after alignment every figure's outline agreement should be high; a missing or extra figure shows as low agreement or unexplained edges.
computable_from: aligned painting, plate facts
proposed_calculation: Per-figure outline agreement (as picture_mismatch) after alignment; flag any figure under 0.6 and any strong edge blob of figure size outside all outlines.
already_automatic: Partly (picture_mismatch flags props that don't line up).
llm_tip: Run the checker on each painting with the plate's facts; a painter that adds or drops a person must be re-asked.

name: Out-of-date or shifted picture detection
how_found: Log 31: a picture made before the scene changed was judged as current. Log 32: brightness-only edges missed a rusty drum on a blue-grey road (lesson 117); colour edges added; the test then found Flux's 3-pixel shift.
final_value_or_rule: Edges: LAB blurred 1.5, Canny 20/60 on lightness and 10/30 on both colour channels, widened 7 x 7. Each story prop (and others over 0.5% of the frame, at least 400 px) is slid up to 1/30 of the width in steps of max(2, W/270) px. Out of date if the best agreement gains at least 0.08 or stays under 0.45 (up-to-date pictures gained 0; moved props gained 0.09 to 0.23).
computable_from: the picture and the facts
proposed_calculation: Already computed; run it on every painting as it arrives and route a failure to align_painting.py.
already_automatic: Yes in check_shot.py (kit and plugin kit).
llm_tip: If the checker says the picture doesn't match the scene, re-render or align the painting before reading any light rule.

name: Colour continuity between paintings of one place
how_found: Plan 34 'One painting chain': W3 painted first as master; every other Works painting gets it as style picture; then a colour check; match_model_colours.py judged only rough (circular, log 22).
final_value_or_rule: Average colour of each factory's brick, roofs, gates and sky inside their outlines, new painting vs master; a clear mismatch means a repaint.
evidence: 34 Plan ... .md 'How the two factories stay the same' point 6; film-kit/paper-film/tools/match_model_colours.py header
computable_from: two aligned paintings and shot_facts masks for each view
proposed_calculation: Per group mean CIELAB inside the visible mask; delta E vs master; flag delta E > 8 (to tune on the first pair).
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: Paint a master view first and pass it as the style picture for every other view of the same place, then compare group colours numerically.

name: Colour rules for real places
how_found: Plan's lettering and colour rules (election on 7 November); round 2 found two red coats were the eye's target.
final_value_or_rule: No large flat areas of a party's, supermarket chain's or bank's colour; hi-vis orange, never yellow-and-black; no banknotes or coins (portraits).
computable_from: plate and filmed still
proposed_calculation: Convert to HSV; flag connected regions over 1.5% of the frame with saturation > 0.45 in listed party/chain hues; check yellow+black stripe patterns.
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: Scan every real-place view for big areas of one strong colour before painting.

name: Meaningful colours and symbols
how_found: Decision 22: a blue tie read as a party colour in an election period; the top-hatted caricature added a claim. Decision 24: the price tag climbs in arrows, not pounds, until the film reaches New Zealand. Lesson 19: placards and flags with real political meaning.
final_value_or_rule: Charcoal, grey or ivory for invented officials; blank placards; no currency before the place is set.
computable_from: page files + cut list
proposed_calculation: Lint currency symbols against the page's place; measure the dominant hue of officials' clothing and flag party colours.
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: Neutral colours for officials, blank placards.

name: Contact sheets before cutting
how_found: Lesson 26: shells came out like rifle cartridges and a tank an odd shape; found on contact sheets before cutting. Lesson 19: video samples added flags and wrong-era tanks.
final_value_or_rule: Check every painting on a contact sheet for history mistakes, symbols and flags before cutting.
computable_from: paintings folder
proposed_calculation: save_fal_paintings.py makes the sheet automatically after each batch, captioned with each request's prompt and the ledger id it shows.
already_automatic: Contact sheet tools exist; not run automatically.
llm_tip: Look at every painting next to what it must show before cutting it.

name: Masks over magenta, and remover repairs
how_found: Lesson 27: the remover dropped the lectern, made Sardinia faint and left a coal heap half see-through. Found by laying cut-outs over magenta. Fixes: lectern from its outline (measured from colours); map printed on a card; lower 'solid' threshold for the pithead.
final_value_or_rule: Every cut-out over magenta before use; thin or island shapes go on a card.
computable_from: painting + mask (objects painted on plain grey)
proposed_calculation: Per mask: pixels differing from the grey background by > 30 levels but with alpha < 0.5 = missing paint; flag if > 1% of the object. Share of alpha between 0.1 and 0.9 inside the hull > 3% = see-through; lower the solid threshold. More than 3 separate pieces = print on a card.
already_automatic: The magenta sheet exists (plugin kit); judging is by eye.
llm_tip: Lay every cut-out over magenta; missing parts show at once.

name: What the background remover drops from cut-outs
how_found: Log 13: laying every cut-out over magenta showed what the remover had dropped: the politician's lectern (put back), Sardinia on the map (the map went on a paper card) and part of a coal heap (kept with a lower threshold). Log 11: a small pale fin that could read as a flag was cut away.
final_value_or_rule: A magenta contact sheet of every cut-out; a threshold per piece in the cut list.
computable_from: the painting and its mask
proposed_calculation: Flag pieces where more than 2% of the pixels that differ from the grey backdrop (by more than 12 levels) fall outside the mask, or where the mask has islands.
already_automatic: contact_sheet_masks.py, which is visual only.
llm_tip: Look at every cut-out over magenta, not over white or grey.

name: Sheet must be bigger than what is drawn on it
how_found: Lesson 38: the oak's sheet was narrower than its crown, so leaves past the edge were missing (cut off in a straight line). Fix: wider sheet, tree shape measured from its height.
final_value_or_rule: Sheet = drawing's bounding box + margin; shape sized from height.
computable_from: the drawn content's alpha bounds
proposed_calculation: Compute the drawing's alpha>0 bounding box and set the sheet to that plus a 4% margin; fail if any drawn pixel touches the sheet edge.
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: Size the sheet from what is drawn, not the other way round.

name: Over-colourful faces and pieces
how_found: Decisions item 25 (user screenshot 1): one face was over-saturated next to the others. tone_piece.py measured it at about 1.7 times as colourful as the other people.
final_value_or_rule: tone_piece defaults: saturation 0.62, contrast 0.9, lift 0.03, the same on every layer of a piece (face, jaw, mouth).
computable_from: all cut-out pieces on a page
proposed_calculation: tone_piece --measure every piece. For any piece whose mean saturation is over 1.2 x the page's median, set saturation = median / piece's own value, and apply the same factor to all its layers.
already_automatic: Measure mode exists (plugin kit); the factor is chosen by hand.
llm_tip: Measure saturation across all people on a page; match the loud one to the median.

name: Colourfulness of painted people and figures
how_found: Log 20: the politician's face was about 1.7 times as colourful as the other painted people; all three layers (face, jaw, mouth) were calmed to match. Log 34 round 2: the figures' coats were too red, with a toy-like look.
final_value_or_rule: tone_piece.py --saturation 0.62 --contrast 0.9 --lift 0.03, the same on every layer of one figure.
computable_from: all pieces and figure materials
proposed_calculation: Measure every piece with tone_piece --measure. For pieces above 1.2 × the median colour strength, saturation factor = median / piece. Apply it to all layers of that figure. For 3D figures, cap saturation at 1.2 × the scene's median.
already_automatic: Measuring yes; the factor is set by hand (tone_piece.py, plugin kit).
llm_tip: Compare every figure's colour strength with the rest before filming.

name: Depth picture spread and blur
how_found: Lesson 41: the built-in distance drawing squeezed near and far into a few shades, and a strong blur turned leaves and hills to mush. Fix: custom depth spread evenly, gentler blur. Workflows: prepare_relief --blur 3.
final_value_or_rule: Even spread of depth values; blur 3 px.
computable_from: depth picture
proposed_calculation: Histogram-equalise depth before use; warn if 90% of pixels fall in under 20 grey levels.
already_automatic: Blur is a parameter; spread isn't checked.
llm_tip: Look at the depth picture's spread before building a relief.

name: Fitting shapes to AI paintings
how_found: Lesson 80: a true rectangle fitted to the canopy missed its painted edges by about 45 px; fit shapes to painted corners. Faces seen nearly edge-on must still wear the painting or they draw dark. Lesson 74: models wearing the projected painting brought back its glow and brushwork. Lesson 75: SAM 3D files have no normals. Lesson 76: fit the ground from around the base.
final_value_or_rule: Fit by painted corners; project the painting onto models; compute normals on load; ground fitted from a ring round the base.
computable_from: painting + masks + depth
proposed_calculation: Already in fit_station_proxies.py and ground_under_objects.py; loader computes normals when missing.
already_automatic: ground_under_objects in the plugin; fit_station_proxies only in the film kit.
llm_tip: AI paintings don't obey perspective; fit to what is painted.

name: Paint-out masks and stand-ins in AI paintings
how_found: Log 24: the canopy wouldn't fit as a rectangle because the painting's perspective isn't consistent, so it was fitted to its four painted corners. Ghosts of a post and the kiosk showed until the painted-out areas were widened. A grey block stood in front of the kiosk until the painted-out part was pushed further back. The canopy's underside drew dark until surfaces seen almost edge-on could wear the painting. Stand-ins drew brighter until both they and the background showed the painting with no lamp.
final_value_or_rule: Match from the painting's view: mean about 4 levels off, 6.4% of pixels more than 12 off (the pass mark). Widen paint-out masks. Fit shapes to painted corners. No lamp on painted surfaces.
computable_from: the painting and the fitted boxes
proposed_calculation: Score automatically: render from the projector's view and compare with the painting; pass if mean difference ≤ 5 levels and share over 12 levels ≤ 7%. Widen masks by the painter's outline width + 4 px.
already_automatic: fit_station_proxies.py and station_plates.py are in the film kit only, not in the plugin kit. No general score.
llm_tip: AI paintings have inconsistent perspective: fit stand-ins to painted corners, not to true rectangles.

name: Keeping the painting's own light on 3D objects
how_found: Logs 22 and 24: one colour over each whole model turned chrome and headlights cyan; colour handling was wrong twice; models drew as black blocks (no surface directions in their files); models floated. The painting's own light is kept exactly; the 3D car and pumps take a small share of the lamp, and their shadows fall on a see-through ground that shows only shadows.
final_value_or_rule: Painted surfaces unlit. 3D objects get a small lamp share. Car colour within a few levels of the painting; pumps about 10% darker.
computable_from: the painting, the model masks and a render from the painting's view
proposed_calculation: Use projected-set's calibrate (draw the set from the projector with and without the painting) and a per-object gain to match the painting inside each mask; two rounds.
already_automatic: Partly: projected-set calibrate (film kit only). match_model_colours.py is superseded (its check was circular).
llm_tip: Work out surface directions when loading models that lack them, and never use one colour over a whole model.

name: State picture thresholds
how_found: Workflows log 34 and make_state_picture.py: thresholds measured on the people test: 6 levels alone left man-shaped shadow ends over 6.8% of the frame; adding a blurred 3-level 'faint' test left under 4 levels everywhere but 0.04%.
final_value_or_rule: --threshold 6, --faint 3 (blurred 10 px), widen 12, soften 5, outline widen 6; PNG only; must equal the main painting outside the mask.
computable_from: both plates + both paintings + outlines
proposed_calculation: Already computed, including a noise re-measure per view (warns if threshold < 3 x noise).
already_automatic: In the film kit only (not in the plugin kit).
llm_tip: Change only what changed: build state pictures from the plates' difference.

name: State-picture mask thresholds
how_found: Round 2 compared thresholds 4, 6, 8, 10 and 14, alone and with a lower threshold for faint smooth changes, and mapped what each left behind; measured render noise (0.2 to 0.6) and JPEG noise (99th percentile 2 after blur).
final_value_or_rule: Blur both plates 2 px; difference = largest colour channel; changed if > 6 levels, or if the 10 px-blurred difference > 3 (faint shadows). Clear specks, widen 12 px, soften 5 px, outline widen 6 px (for a 1536-wide plate; scales with width). 6 alone left 6.8% of the frame > 3 levels off; 10 alone left 0.48% > 8; chosen settings leave 0.04% > 4. Tool warns if a threshold is under 3 x measured noise.
computable_from: plate and helper plate, figure outlines
proposed_calculation: Keep as is; also print the swap area at 4/6/8 and faint 2/3/4 for the view so the choice is visible.
already_automatic: Yes (make_state_picture.py, film kit only).
llm_tip: Use threshold 6 and faint 3, then look at the mask picture before trusting it.

name: State picture mask thresholds (make_state_picture.py)
how_found: Round 2 of log 34 (people test): two renders of the same set differ under 1 level (99th percentile 0.2 to 0.6), JPEG adds up to 2; with 6 levels alone, man-shaped shadow ends (3 to 8 levels) stayed over 6.8% of the frame; 10 levels left 8 to 12; adding a smooth 3-level difference left under 4 levels except 0.04%.
final_value_or_rule: Difference = largest channel after a 2 px blur; changed if over 6 levels, or if the 10 px-blurred difference is over 3. Specks opened by a 1.5 px disc, pieces under 60 px squared dropped, gaps closed by a 6 px disc; outlines widened 6; mask widened 12 then softened 5 (all for a 1536-wide plate, scaled by width/1536). Warn if a threshold is under 3 times the measured noise (99th percentile fine grain in the quarter of the frame furthest from the change).
computable_from: the plate and helper plate
proposed_calculation: Already computed; make the noise measurement choose the thresholds automatically: threshold = max(6, 3*noise), faint = max(3, 3*noise_smooth).
already_automatic: Tool in the kit only (not in the plugin kit).
llm_tip: Make state pictures from the two plates' difference plus the changing things' outlines; check the --look picture before trusting it.

name: State picture mask thresholds (make_state_picture.py)
how_found: Log 34 round 2: measured render noise (99th pct 0.2-0.6 levels) and JPEG noise (up to 2); 6 levels alone left man-shaped shadow ends over 6.8% of the frame; adding a 10-px-blurred difference down to 3 levels left < 4 levels everywhere but 0.04%. JPEG output changed every pixel (0.48 avg, up to 9) so output is lossless.
final_value_or_rule: --threshold 6, --faint 3 (on a 10 px blur), plates blurred 2 px first, max of RGB channels, --widen 12, --soften 5, --outline-widen 6; output PNG/lossless WebP; residual outside mask must be exactly 0; warns if threshold < 3x measured noise.
computable_from: main painting, second painting, plate, helper plate, figure outlines
proposed_calculation: Already self-calibrating (noise measured per view); expose the printed coverage table in the plugin skill.
already_automatic: Yes, in the film kit; missing from the plugin kit.
llm_tip: Make every state change with make_state_picture.py, never by swapping the whole painting: only what changed may change.

name: State pictures are lossless and read back exactly
how_found: Round 2 check: writing the state picture as JPEG 93 moved the whole frame 0.48 levels on average and up to 9 outside the mask.
final_value_or_rule: Write PNG or lossless WebP only (JPEG refused); read back; largest difference from the main painting where the mask is zero must be 0 levels (stops otherwise).
evidence: make_state_picture.py docstring lines 41-46; round2-result.json checked.findings[8]; round3-result.json fixes.summary
computable_from: the files
proposed_calculation: Already automatic.
already_automatic: Yes (film kit only).
llm_tip: Never save a state picture or a painting used for one as JPEG.

name: State pictures must be lossless and exact outside the mask
how_found: Round 2: saving again as JPEG changed every pixel (0.48 levels on average, up to 9 outside the mask).
final_value_or_rule: Write PNG (compression 6) or lossless WebP (quality 101); read back; the largest difference from the main painting where the mask is 0 must be 0 levels, else stop. Paintings used as main paintings are kept as PNG too.
evidence: make_state_picture.py lines 70-71, 124-127, 194-225; make_behind_picture.py lines 78-79, 100-106; people-test-paintings.json kept_lossless
computable_from: file type
proposed_calculation: Automatic; extend the rule to every painting saved for the film.
already_automatic: Yes inside both tools (kit only).
llm_tip: Never save a painting or state picture as JPEG once it is used as a base.

name: Second paintings differ everywhere: swap only inside a mask
how_found: Round 1 check: the free test swapped the whole picture; with two real paintings every brushstroke would change at the cut. People test paintings: the two paintings differ by 8.5 levels on average outside the mask.
final_value_or_rule: Never cut to a whole second painting; a state picture = main painting outside the mask + second painting inside it. Paid test mask: 38.3% fully plus 8.2% partly.
computable_from: two paintings, two plates
proposed_calculation: make_state_picture.py (below); assert the cut swaps no pixel outside the mask.
already_automatic: Yes in the film kit (make_state_picture.py); not in the plugin kit.
llm_tip: For a change on a word, swap only the area that changes; a whole new painting flickers every brushstroke.

name: Changes on a held shot (state pictures)
how_found: Log 34: changes on a held shot (the men gone, the windows lit) are made by swapping only the area that changes. Measured on the people test's plates: two renders of the same set differ by under 1 level of grain.
final_value_or_rule: make_state_picture.py: a pixel counts as changed if, after a 2 px blur, its largest colour difference is over 6 levels, or over 3 levels after a 10 px blur. The mask is cleared of specks, widened, then softened.
computable_from: two plates (with and without the change) and the outlines
proposed_calculation: Already a calculation.
already_automatic: In the film kit only. make_state_picture.py and make_behind_picture.py are NOT in the plugin kit.
llm_tip: Never cut to a whole second painting: every brushstroke would jump.

name: Cut or blend, from the size of the change
how_found: Swap areas measured every round: people test 42% (long shadows); Works round 3 men gone 6.5 to 8%, slowed 5.2 to 6.5%, working 41 to 50%; round 4 men gone 9.3%, slowed 8.5%, behind 5.6%, working 75.7% once No. 1's beam lit the lane.
final_value_or_rule: A time cut where the mask is small (about 10% or less: the men going); a blend (0.8 to 1.5 s) where it is large (windows lighting, 41 to 76%). States reached by a cut keep the spill lights of the state before, so plates differ only where the men stood.
evidence: round3-result.json works.summary and NOT DONE 'working state picture swaps 41%'; round4-result.json set.summary 'State pictures'; assemble_works.py lines 222-230 (STATES note on spill)
computable_from: plate pairs per change, script events
proposed_calculation: area = mask share; if area <= 0.12 -> time cut; else blend over 0.8 s + 0.7 s x (area/0.75); warn if a cut is asked for over 0.12. Check that lights not tied to the change have identical settings in both plates.
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: Cut when only a small part of the frame changes; blend when the light over much of it changes; keep every other light identical between the two plates.

name: One helper plate per separately timed change
how_found: Round 3 effects: 'go' needed W1 'men gone, windows still dark' or the mask couldn't keep the windows dark until 'start'. Round 3 pages: No. 1's doorway lit as soon as the slide started (behind picture had it lit) -> 'quiet, no men' plate. Round 4 pages: one slowed picture held both the dark windows and the men, so a window blend on 'slows' would fade the men in as ghosts -> needs a windows-only slowed picture.
final_value_or_rule: Every change that happens on its own word needs its own plate pair: men gone (windows dark), working (windows lit), quiet-no-men (behind picture), slowed-windows-only, slowed-with-men.
evidence: round3-result.json effects.summary 'One more helper plate'; round3-result.json pages.summary item 2; round4-result.json pageFixes.summary 'One thing page 12 will need'
computable_from: script events (state changes and their words) per view
proposed_calculation: From the page events, list per view the ordered state changes; each distinct (view, state after change k) needs a plate; derive the plate list and the state-picture commands automatically; flag a state change that bundles two changes timed on different words.
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: List every change on its own word and give each its own plate; one plate holding two changes makes the earlier one ghost in.

name: Behind picture is the same state as the main picture
how_found: Round 3 pages: during page 3's slide No. 1's doorway lit up as soon as the camera moved, long before 'go', because the behind picture came from the working plate.
final_value_or_rule: The behind picture (shown where near things stood once the camera moves) is made from a plate of the same state with only the near things left out ('quiet, no men'); swap area 5.6 to 5.7%.
evidence: round3-result.json pages.summary item 2; assemble_works.py STATES 'quiet, no men' lines 243-246
computable_from: view's main state
proposed_calculation: For each sliding view: behind plate = main state with the near story things hidden; check the behind mask touches only areas behind those things.
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: Make the behind picture from the same state as the main one, minus the near things, or hidden parts change early.

name: Behind picture by filling in (make_behind_picture.py)
how_found: Round 3 of log 34: using another picture of the view as the behind picture also lit windows and a doorway behind the waiting men the moment the slide began.
final_value_or_rule: Main painting everywhere except inside the near things' outlines widened 10 px, filled from round about (OpenCV Telea, radius 9), sizes for a 1536-wide plate; written as PNG and checked 0 levels off outside. A state picture from a helper plate drawn without the near things is truer when one exists.
computable_from: the main painting and near outlines
proposed_calculation: Automatic when no helper plate exists for the near things; otherwise use make_state_picture.py with that helper plate.
already_automatic: Tool in kit only (not in the plugin kit).
llm_tip: For the behind picture use a fill of the same painting, never a different painting of the view.

name: Time cut is the default; fade only as fallback
how_found: Plan T9; round 3 and 4 tested the go=swing fallback: men see-through for about a second while fading.
final_value_or_rule: Default: a time cut on the spoken word to the state picture; fallback: gate swings in 0.8 s and men fade in 1.2 s inside the swing (two set draws). A state changes only while the camera holds; cards may change during a slide.
evidence: PLAN lines 132-143 and 1467; round4-result.json pageFixes.summary item 5
computable_from: script events, camera moves
proposed_calculation: Reject any state change scheduled inside a slide's time span; schedule cuts on the named word's start time.
already_automatic: No (camera_audit.py checks the camera, not state timing).
llm_tip: People vanish by a cut on the word, never by a fade, and only while the camera is still.

name: Keep state changes small: no long shadows from things that come and go
how_found: Round 2: the people-test mask covered 42% of the frame (32% at 6 levels alone) because the men's long shadows and the fire light they blocked changed. Round 3: men drawn casting no long shadows with a small soft patch at their feet: mask 7% (W1 men gone) and 5% (W2 slowed). Plates fell from 25 to about 6 minutes when only the fire, the lit doorways and the sky cast shadows.
final_value_or_rule: Things that come and go cast no long shadows and don't block the fire's light; each gets a small soft shadow at its feet; helper plates keep the yards' lighting the same as the main plate. Flag a mask over about 15% (W1 working swapped 76% at 'start', round 4).
evidence: round2-result.json; round3-result.json 'State pictures' and 'Speed'; round4-result.json finding 15; make_state_picture.py docstring lines 44-46
computable_from: which groups differ between the two states and which lights cast shadows on them
proposed_calculation: Before rendering a helper plate: turn off shadow casting for the changing groups (Blender visible_shadow false) and add contact shadows; predict the mask as outlines widened 12 px; after rendering, fail if the mask exceeds 15% of the frame.
already_automatic: No; done by hand in the Works scripts.
llm_tip: Draw people and other changing things without cast shadows, or the time cut will swap half the painting.

name: People and their long shadows; the state area must stay small
how_found: People test (log 34): the painter left the men's long shadows when asked to remove them and the swap area grew to 46% of the frame for people covering 6% (round 2: 42%). Plates were redrawn with no long shadows from the men (a small soft patch at their feet). Lesson 135.
final_value_or_rule: Figures cast no long shadows from fire or lamps in plates; foot shadow patch only; state mask should cover little more than the figures and feet.
evidence: works-shot.json decisions.men_shadows; make_state_picture.py docstring ('Cost'); round2-result.json finding 17
computable_from: plate and helper plate, figure outlines (shot_facts)
proposed_calculation: make_state_picture.py already prints mask coverage; add a ratio check: mask area / figure-outline area <= 3, else warn 'figures throw shadows or block light'; in the Blender assembly set cast_shadow False for figures on every light except a foot-patch.
already_automatic: Coverage is printed by make_state_picture.py (film kit only); the ratio rule and shadow switch are manual.
llm_tip: Switch off figures' shadows from scene lights before drawing plates; give each a soft foot shadow instead.

name: Which groups to pass as --outlines for a state picture
how_found: Works check files for each state (w1 quiet vs w1 working: men 1 to 7 vs 'people at work' and 'pop-up crates').
final_value_or_rule: The groups present in one state and absent or changed in the other, measured for the plate's own camera and lens (shot_facts.py --fov plate lens).
computable_from: the two states' check files
proposed_calculation: outlines = symmetric difference of the two check files' group lists, plus groups whose facts (position, visible area) differ by more than 1%.
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: Derive the outline groups by comparing the two states' check files; measure them with the plate's lens.

name: The window group that flickers must be in the frame
how_found: Round 3 check: No. 2's mill windows were not in W2's frame at all (the gable had a loft door), so 'windows blazing' could not be seen. Round 4 replaced the loft door with three tall mill windows in the window groups.
final_value_or_rule: Each state's visible cue (lit windows, smoke, gate) must project inside the frame, below the title band, in every view that shows that state.
computable_from: window group bounding boxes, camera, script states per view
proposed_calculation: For each (view, state) list the cue objects; project their boxes; require at least 60% of each cue's area inside [0, 1] x [title bottom, 1] at the composed spot.
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: For every word that changes a picture, check the thing that changes is actually inside that view's frame.

name: Show people at work where the story says 'flat out' or 'they go in'
how_found: Round 4 critic: both lit doorways showed an empty cream room; the men vanished at 'go' but never appeared inside; the flat-out factory read 'open late or deserted'. Round 5 added workers.
final_value_or_rule: Two dark figures at the machines inside each lit doorway (No. 2 in every No. 2 plate, one in the slowed state; No. 1 only in the working and men-gone plates), from behind or side-on, cloth 0.025/0.024/0.026, 17 m or more from every camera (heads 20 to 24 px), spill lights linked to skip them so they stay dark against the lit back wall.
evidence: round5-set/tools/new_layout.txt WORKERS; assemble_works.py lines 959-973 and 1206-1212; round4-result.json critique.findings[0]
computable_from: script (which states need 'busy' or 'going in'), scene
proposed_calculation: From the script's state list, any state described as busy or working must contain at least one figure inside a lit area of the frame; check its projected head <= 24 px and its luminance below the lit wall behind it by a ratio of at least 3.
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: If the words say people are working, show a dark figure at a machine; an empty lit room reads as deserted.

name: Windows in step groups; no merged glow
how_found: Plan F4 (build_factory merged all windows); round 2 built separate panes in three named thirds per factory.
final_value_or_rule: Every pane its own piece in groups <prefix>-windows-step-1 to 3 (No. 1: 25, 23, 26; No. 2: 26, 27, 27 plus the doorway); lit and dark glass materials kept; windows change in steps, the set redrawn once per step.
evidence: round2-result.json factories.summary and tested; works-effects.js header
computable_from: script states (fractions lit)
proposed_calculation: Split panes into N groups by x order where N = the number of distinct lit fractions in the script's states.
already_automatic: Yes in build_factories.py (film kit).
llm_tip: Build windows as separate panes in groups so they can light in steps without a new painting.

name: A time cut of people alone reads as a glitch
how_found: People test (log 34): a first-time viewer read the men blinking out as a fault; nothing else changed and the fire even looked bigger. Lesson 136. Fix in the Works: men appear working inside, windows light, chimney smokes.
final_value_or_rule: Something else must change with the people (light later, fire lower, the people seen elsewhere); fallback a 1.2 s blend inside a 0.8 s gate swing in 6 steps.
evidence: Lessons 136; page-3.js (inflation-chapter-2-newcomers) GO 'swing' fallback; 34 Plan 'How the men come and go'
computable_from: judgement only (a planning rule)
proposed_calculation: Planning checklist only: for each state change listed in the shot list, require at least one non-figure change in the same moment.
already_automatic: No.
llm_tip: When people vanish on a cut, change something else in the same frame so it reads as time passing.
